Altivon Builders, team of passionate developers, AI/ML innovators, and space enthusiasts on a mission to make astronomical discovery more accessible.

We are building an interactive SPHEREx Planet Explorer that transforms NASA's astronomical observations into an engaging sky exploration platform. By combining AI-powered candidate detection, time-series analysis, multi-band visualization, and intelligent data exploration, we aim to help users uncover celestial patterns and identify moving objects
summary:
SPHEREx Planet X is an astronomical data analysis platform that transforms real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations into interactive time-series visualizations with AI-assisted scientific interpretation.

The platform integrates NASA's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) through its Simple Image Access (SIA) service, using Astroquery to retrieve observations based on Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates.

Built with Python and FastAPI, the backend processes Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) files using Astropy and NumPy. Its pipeline performs epoch deduplication, temporal frame selection, FITS HDU extraction, bitmask-aware FLAGS quality assessment, and percentile-based image normalization. IRSA's cutout service retrieves spatially cropped observations, which are converted into optimized WebP frames and stored through disk caching.

The React and TypeScript frontend provides an interactive flipbook with playback controls, frame navigation, and URL-based observation sharing. AI integration through OpenRouter and Gemini-compatible models generates astrophysical interpretations and enables multi-turn conversational analysis.

By combining astronomical data retrieval, FITS processing, temporal visualization, and generative AI, SPHEREx Planet X simplifies the exploration and analysis of real infrared observations.
details:
SPHEREx Planet X – Project Details

1. Project Overview

SPHEREx Planet X is an AI-assisted astronomical exploration platform designed to make NASA's SPHEREx infrared observations easier to retrieve, process, visualize, and interpret. It addresses the challenge of accessing and understanding complex astronomical datasets that are traditionally distributed in large FITS (Flexible Image Transport System) files requiring specialized scientific software and technical expertise.

Our platform transforms these observations into interactive time-series flipbooks, allowing users to investigate how celestial objects appear across different observation epochs. It combines astronomical data engineering, scientific image processing, interactive visualization, and generative AI within a unified web application.

2. How Does It Work?

The platform follows an integrated data-processing pipeline:

Step 1 – Astronomical Coordinate Input

Users provide Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates to identify a region or celestial target in the sky. The platform also supports predefined astronomical targets, including WISE 0855.

Step 2 – NASA Data Retrieval

The backend communicates with NASA's Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) through its Simple Image Access (SIA) service using Astroquery. It retrieves SPHEREx observation metadata and corresponding Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) file references.

Step 3 – FITS Processing and Data Optimization

Using Astropy and NumPy, the system processes astronomical FITS data, extracts image information from the relevant HDUs, identifies unique observation epochs, and performs temporal frame selection. It also incorporates bitmask-aware FLAGS analysis for data-quality assessment and percentile-based intensity normalization.

Instead of downloading complete MEF files, the system uses IRSA's cutout service to retrieve spatially cropped observations, significantly reducing data-transfer requirements.

Step 4 – Image Rendering and Flipbook Generation

The extracted astronomical images are normalized and converted into optimized WebP frames using Pillow. These frames are stored through disk-based caching to reduce repeated downloads and processing time.

Step 5 – Interactive Visualization

The React and TypeScript frontend displays the processed observations through an interactive flipbook. Users can play, pause, adjust playback speed, navigate individual frames, and explore observations across different time periods. URL-based sharing also allows observations to be accessed through shared coordinate links.

Step 6 – AI-Assisted Scientific Interpretation

The platform integrates OpenRouter and Gemini-compatible AI models to generate astrophysical interpretations of observations. Its conversational interface supports multi-turn questions, allowing users to investigate the data and explore its potential scientific significance.

3. Technologies and Tools Used

Backend and Scientific Computing

  • Python 3.11 – Core data-processing language.
  • FastAPI – REST API development and asynchronous request handling.
  • Astropy – Astronomical FITS file processing.
  • Astroquery – Integration with NASA IRSA services.
  • NumPy – Numerical operations and image-array processing.
  • Pillow – Image normalization and WebP conversion.
  • HTTPX – External service communication and AI requests.

Frontend and Visualization

  • React 18 and TypeScript – Interactive application development.
  • Vite – Frontend development and build tooling.
  • Tailwind CSS – Interface styling.
  • Zustand – Centralized application state management.
  • Chart.js – Charting capabilities.

AI and Infrastructure

  • OpenRouter – AI model integration and provider routing.
  • Gemini-compatible models – Astronomical interpretation and conversational analysis.
  • GitHub Actions – Automated testing and CI/CD.
  • Render – Application deployment.

4. Innovation and Creativity

The key innovation is the transformation of static, technically complex astronomical observations into a time-based visual exploration experience.

Rather than simply displaying individual FITS images, SPHEREx Planet X connects multiple observation epochs into an interactive flipbook. This allows users to explore temporal changes in observations through a single interface.

The integration of AI adds another layer of exploration by translating astronomical observations into understandable scientific explanations. Combining real NASA observational data, optimized image processing, temporal visualization, and conversational AI creates a more approachable method of investigating infrared astronomy.

5. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Accessibility: Reduces the technical barrier to exploring astronomical datasets.
  • Data efficiency: Spatial cutouts reduce unnecessary downloads and processing overhead.
  • Scientific exploration: Enables visual investigation of observations across multiple epochs.
  • AI-assisted understanding: Helps users interpret astronomical observations without requiring extensive prior expertise.
  • Reusability: Coordinate-based queries allow the platform to be used for different astronomical targets.
  • Citizen science: Encourages students, researchers, and astronomy enthusiasts to engage with real NASA datasets.

6. Project Validation and Future Potential

For our WISE 0855 demonstration, the pipeline retrieved 278 SPHEREx MEF references, identified 142 unique observation epochs spanning approximately 362 days, and selected frames for interactive visualization. Spatial cutouts reduced the data-transfer requirement from approximately 70 MB for a full MEF to around 5 MB per cutout.

The platform establishes a foundation for further development, including multi-target comparison, spectral visualization across SPHEREx's 102 infrared bands, astronomical catalog overlays, and automated candidate investigation.

Our long-term vision is to bridge astronomical data science and public exploration by making real infrared observations more interactive, interpretable, and useful for scientific discovery.
